title: In the Matter of TRISO-X, LLC; Confirmatory Order Modifying License
summary: The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) is issuing a Confirmatory Order to TRISO-X, LLC (the licensee), as a result of a successful Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) mediation. On June 9, 2026, the NRC notified the licensee of an apparent violation being considered for escalated enforcement. The apparent violation involved the implementation of management measures to ensure the design basis supporting the structural stability function of the TX-1 process building's main force resisting system (MFRS) was maintained during construction. The NRC provided the licensee with the opportunity to respond through a written response, a Pre-decisional Enforcement Conference (PEC), or ADR. The licensee elected to participate in ADR, and mediation sessions were held on July 29 and August 20, 2026, during which the parties reached an Agreement in Principle. As part of the agreement, the licensee committed to taking certain corrective actions and consented to the issuance of a Confirmatory Order to make those commitments legally binding and resolve the apparent violation without further enforcement action by the NRC. The Confirmatory Order is effective upon issuance.

summary: The FAA proposes to supersede Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2015-17-10, which applies to certain SOCATA (type certificate currently held by Daher Aircraft, SAS) (Daher) Model TBM 700 airplanes. AD 2015- 17-10 requires repetitively inspecting the forging body of the main landing gear (MLG) for cracks and, depending on findings, performing corrective actions. AD 2015-17-10 allows for replacement of affected MLG with a reinforced landing gear as a terminating action for repetitive inspections. Since the FAA issued AD 2015-17-10, additional MLG serviceable parts have been developed, and it has been determined that dye penetrant is no longer an authorized inspection method. This proposed AD would continue to require the actions of AD 2015-17-10, add the additional serviceable parts, and eliminate the option of using dye penetrant as an inspection method. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.

title: Marine Mammals; Proposed Incidental Harassment Authorization for the Southern Beaufort Sea Stock of Polar Bears During Exploration Activities in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge 1002 Area Alaska; Draft Environmental Assessment
issuer: Interior Department; Fish and Wildlife Service
summary: We, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, in response to a request under the Marine Mammal Protection Act from the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA), propose to authorize nonlethal incidental take by harassment of small numbers of Southern Beaufort Sea (SBS) polar bears (Ursus maritimus) for 1 year from the date of issuance of the incidental harassment authorization (IHA). The applicant requested this authorization for take by harassment that may result from activities associated with a seismic exploration program in the Coastal Plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge Section 1002 area. This proposed authorization, if finalized, will be take of polar bears associated with the specified activities, which may come from the SBS stock. We invite comments on the proposed IHA and accompanying draft environmental assessment from the public, Tribes, and local, State, and Federal agencies.
